entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ne 5:1-5 . The People Complain of Their Debt, Mortgage, and Bondage.

entries.heading: 14. Moreover from the time that I was appointed . . . I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor
entries.text: 14. Moreover from the time that I was appointed . . . I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor --We have a remarkable proof both of the opulence and the disinterestedness of Nehemiah. As he declined, on conscientious grounds, to accept the lawful emoluments attached to his government, and yet maintained a style of princely hospitality for twelve years out of his own resources, it is evident that his office of cup-bearer at the court of Shushan must have been very lucrative.

entries.heading: 15. the former governors . . . had taken . . . bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver
entries.text: 15. the former governors . . . had taken . . . bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver --The income of Eastern governors is paid partly in produce, partly in money. "Bread" means all sorts of provision. The forty shekels of silver per day would amount to a yearly salary of £1800 sterling.

entries.heading: 17. Moreover there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the Jews
entries.text: 17. Moreover there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the Jews --In the East it has been always customary to calculate the expense of a king's or grandee's establishment, not by the amount of money disbursed, but by the quantity of provisions consumed (see 1Ki 4:22; 18:19; Ec 5:11 ).
